god_almighty_unknown_language.description: An unnamed language used by the Ancient Sun God
god_almighty_unknown_language.notes: Similar to Jotun but different. Not Elvish, Dragonese, or Ancient Hermes. Has similarities with Ancient Feysac and Dutanese.

elvish.description: Ancient language created by the Elf King in the Sprouting Era
elvish.characteristics: Every word is rich in meaning; sentences are very short
elvish.notes: According to Elvin Legend, first-generation elves are born with every word produced

dragonese.description: Ancient language created by Dragons in the Sprouting Era
dragonese.characteristics: Grammatical habit of using short, simple sentences

jotun.description: Ancient language created by Giants in the Sprouting Era
jotun.notes: Still used as a common language in the Forsaken Land of the Gods by the Fifth Epoch. Foundation of Ancient Feysac language.

devil_language.description: Language created by Devils in the Sprouting Era

ancient_hermes.description: Human extraordinary language based on Jotun and Dragonese
ancient_hermes.characteristics: Tongue-twisting language; direct and effective effects

hermes.description: Simplified version of Ancient Hermes developed in the Fourth Epoch
hermes.characteristics: Easier to learn and disseminate; less powerful direct ritual effects than Ancient Hermes
hermes.notes: The language that must be mastered by Beyonders; universally used by Spirit World denizens

other_mystical_languages.description: Specialized languages for specific pathways and domains

pre_epoch_languages.description: Modern era human languages from Earth
pre_epoch_languages.notes: Lost after the First Epoch; only known by transmigrators and certain deities

ancient_feysac.description: Common language of the Fourth Epoch
ancient_feysac.characteristics: Derived from Jotun; has some mystical properties but cannot use natural forces
ancient_feysac.notes: Root language of all contemporary Northern Continent languages

loenese.description: Official language of the Loen Kingdom
loenese.primary_users: Loen Kingdom, Klein Moretti, most Tarot Club members

intisian.description: Official language of the Intis Republic
intisian.characteristics: No mystical properties; represented by French in English translations

feysac.description: Official language of the Feysac Empire
feysac.characteristics: Language with the least difference from Ancient Feysac
feysac.example_phrase: 'Lærdal (洛达尔)' in the local language of Nas means 'Dawn'

highlander.description: Official language of the Feynapotter Kingdom
highlander.notes: Feynapotter Kingdom venerates Earth Mother despite frequent use of sun-related words

lenburg.origin: Essentially same as Highlander with dialectal differences

highlander_southern.description: Original language of the Southern Continent
highlander_southern.status: Equal in status to Ancient Feysac but separate origin

special_terms.'Kadiev': Word for 'King' in ancient Highlands Kingdom; translated by Roselle Gustav as 'Pharaoh'

highlander_southern.notes: Means 'son of God, king of humans'

dutanese.description: Original language of the Southern Continent
dutanese.usage: Common language of the ancient Balam Empire; still used in East and West Balam
dutanese.characteristics: Similar to Ancient Feysac in many ways, as if from same origin, but not Jotun

western_continent.description: Common language of the Western Continent
western_continent.characteristics: Highly similar to Simplified Chinese in grammar and words
western_continent.notes: Mainland Chinese Transmigrators can easily understand it; communication has been maintained across Epochs
western_continent.example_quote: "Imperial brother, please lend me your strength!" - Roselle Gustav inside the Nation of Disorder

trivia.game_connection: The Lord of the Mysteries game introduced the Hermes alphabet, used in the theme song 'Praise The Fool'
trivia.fan_work: Standard Hermes grammar is still being decrypted by fans
